spec.full_target:
The complete Theorem 1 (Logarithm-free convergence), with its Section 2 standing definitions and fixed scheme, on PDF page 2.

Use the periodic domain mathbbT = reals/(2*pi*integers) with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). For a periodic function f, hat f(k) = (2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx and <k> = (1+k^2)^(1/2). The Sobolev norm is ||f||_(H^s)^2 = sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s) |hat f(k)|^2. These spaces are completions of trigonometric polynomials in these norms, with negative-order spaces interpreted as distributions. Reality means hat f(-k) = conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0) = 0. Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms use essential suprema.

Let S_t = exp(-t*partial_x^3), with Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3). Let P0 be the spatial mean and P = I-P0. Let D^(-1) = partial_x^(-1) have multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k != 0 and zero at k=0, and D^(-2) = (D^(-1))^2. The equation is
  u_t + u_xxx = (1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0.
The exact solution is the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation.

For timestep tau=T/L, the time-semidiscrete scheme is exactly
  u^0 = u0,
  u^(n+1) = S_tau u^n + F_tau(u^n) + H_tau(u^n),
where all products below are spatial products and [G(s)]_(s=0)^(s=tau) means G(tau)-G(0):
  F_tau(f) = (1/6)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)^2]
             - (1/6)*S_tau P[(D^(-1) f)^2],
  H_tau(f) = (1/3)*P[(S_tau D^(-1) f)*D^(-1) F_tau(f)]
             + (tau/9)*(S_tau D^(-1) f)*P0(f^2)
             - (1/54)*[S_(tau-s) D^(-1)[(S_s D^(-1) f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)
             - (1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) D^(-2)[(S_(s-tau) D^(-2) F_tau(f))*(S_s D^(-1) f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau).
This is the source scheme (2), with no spatial frequency cutoff.

For every T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0, there exist C>0 and tau0>0 depending only on T,gamma,R such that, for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R and every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0, this fixed scheme satisfies
  max_(0<=n<=L) ||u(n*tau)-u^n||_(L^2) <= C*tau^gamma.
The constants are uniform over the entire stated initial-data ball and all permitted timesteps, with no Fourier-support restriction. The target includes all the hypotheses, quantifiers, endpoints, solution convention and method above.
spec.conclusion: There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.

definitions.definition: KdV is the equation u_t+partial_x^3 u=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2) on mathbbT. For a real mean-zero datum q in H^s, s>=0, and horizon A>0, an exact solution u with datum q means the real mean-zero C([0,A];H^s) distributional solution of this equation with u(0)=q obtained by smooth approximation. An exact twisted solution v means v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) for this same equation and interval. A smooth exact solution means such a solution with smooth space and time dependence. These terms specify a solution relation only; existence, uniqueness, bounds and the differential equation for the twist are proved, rather than granted by this definition.

For the real mean-zero 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, with normalized homogeneous norms, the following results hold in its norm-preserving twisted representation. For every s>=0, time horizon A>0 and L2 upper bound B0, Galerkin solutions with datum q in dot H^s and ||q||_2<=B0 obey sup_[0,A]||U_m||_(dot H^s)<=M_s, uniformly in m, with M_s depending only on s,A,B0,||q||_(dot H^s). For s>0 and 0<sigma<s, a subsequence converges strongly in L^p([0,A];H^sigma), 1<p<infinity, and weak-star in L^infty dot H^s to a distributional solution with the same bound and L2 conservation a.e.. This solution is unique, is C([0,A];dot H^s), preserves L2 at every time and depends Lipschitz continuously on the datum for s>1/2, and also for 0<s<=1/2. At s=0 there is a unique C([0,A];L2) solution with Lipschitz dependence obtained by smoothing. For theta in (-1,0] and two data q,r in L2 whose norms sum to at most B0, the two twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,A]||Utw-Vtw||_(dot H^theta)<=C' C_(B0)^A ||q-r||_(dot H^theta), where C',C_(B0) depend only on B0,theta.

propositions.statement: For T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0 there is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero datum q in H^gamma with ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma) distributional solution u of u_t+u_xxx=u*u_x, obtained by smooth approximation, and sup_[0,T]||u||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth data give spatially smooth solutions on [0,T]. For two real mean-zero L2 data q,r of norms summing to at most B0, the exact solutions satisfy sup_[0,T]||u_q-u_r||_2<=C(T,B0)||q-r||_2. Twisting v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) preserves all Sobolev norms and for smooth data v'=B_t(v,v)/2. Consequently M=1+sup_[0,T]||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A uniformly on the datum ball.

For every tau>0 and real alpha,beta, eta_tau=0 if either phase is zero. Otherwise |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=2 min(|alpha/beta|,|beta/alpha|) and |eta_tau(alpha,beta)|<=tau min(|alpha|,|beta|). For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0 let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the ordered absolute values, A=|ab| and B0=|cd|. Then N1<=3*N2, |d|^(-1)min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3/N3 and |a+b|/max(A,B0)<=6/N3.

The same bound holds upon restricting the positive sum to any subset; C is absolute.

For every exponent s in [0,1], tau>0, nonnegative n and mean-zero f_j in H^s, R2_(n,tau) extends uniquely from polynomials to a trilinear map into L2 with ||R2_(n,tau)(f1,f2,f3)||_2<=C_s*tau^(1+s) product_j ||f_j||_(H^s), uniformly in n,tau and spectral support. The same estimate holds with any multiplier of modulus at most one in the defining sum, including separate restrictions to Phi=0 and Phi!=0. In particular, for 0<gamma<=1, ||w||_(H^gamma)<=M, f mean zero in L2, delta=||f-w||_2<=1 and 0<tau<=1, ||R2_(n,tau)(f,f,f)||_2<=C_(M,gamma)*tau*(tau^gamma+delta), with no H^gamma assumption on f.

propositions.statement: S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality and zero mean. On mean-zero inputs, uniformly in real t: ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infty<=C||f||_2; ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-23/14))<=C||f||_2||g||_2; ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For every A0 in H^1, ||A0||_infty<=C||A0||_(H^1). For A0,B0 in H^1, ||A0 B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1). Also ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2, ||A0||_(H^(-23/14))<=||Dinv A0||_2 for mean-zero A0, and ||J_t(A0,B0)||_2<=C||Dinv A0||_2||B0||_2 whenever the right side is defined. For smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Moreover J is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=Cint_I(f,g,h). These identities hold stepwise for piecewise smooth paths, and Stage_(n,tau)(t;f)=[J_s(f,f)]_(s=n*tau)^t/6.

Uniformly over its step: ||F_n||_(H^1)<=C_M, ||F_n-Stage(t;w)||_(H^1)<=C_M delta, ||F_n||_(H^a_gamma)+||F_n||_2<=C_M q, ||z_n||_X<=C_M, ||B_t(F_n,F_n)||_2<=C_M q, ||Q_n||_2+||W_n||_2<=C_M tau q, ||Dinv Y_n||_2<=C_M tau q, ||Dinv Y_n'||_2<=C_M q, ||Y_n||_2<=C_M q, ||Y_n||_X<=C_M q and ||Y_n||_(H^(-23/14))<=C_M tau q. There exist C>0 and tau0>0, depending only on T,gamma,R, such that for every real mean-zero u0 in H^gamma(mathbbT) with ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, the unique distributional solution u in C([0,T];H^gamma) obtained by smooth approximation and the fixed unfiltered iterates of Psi satisfy max_(0<=n<=L)||u(n*tau)-u^n||_L2<=C*tau^gamma for every positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. The constants are uniform over that entire datum ball and all these L; no Fourier-support restriction is imposed.

argument.text: Fix a real mean-zero q in H^gamma and assume L1: ||q||_(H^gamma)<=R. H001-H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Use E001 for source datum U0(x)=-q(-x), exponent s=gamma and horizon T. Reflection and sign preserve the Fourier Sobolev and L2 norms, so ||U0||_(dot H^gamma)<=R and ||U0||_2<=R. The source yields a global unique continuous flow, its uniform Sobolev bound, and smooth flows when the datum is smooth (apply its positive regularity statements for each integer exponent in that case). Its Galerkin bound and limiting-solution bound are uniform for the prescribed norm bounds.

produces.statement: For the source datum U0(x)=-q(-x) there is a unique continuous homogeneous H^gamma source flow U on [0,T], with uniform bound determined only by T,gamma,R; for smooth q it has every Sobolev regularity.

binders.type: source solution path whose existence is asserted

argument.text: Take that source flow U and set u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). At (t,-x), u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx, so u_t+u_xxx=-U U_x=u*u_x. Fourier coefficients are hat u(k)=-hat U(-k), preserving reality, zero mean and every Fourier norm. On mean-zero functions and s>=0, |k|<=<k><=sqrt(2)|k|, hence ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s); for s<0 the inequalities reverse as in the supplied norm convention. The source bound therefore gives some A(T,gamma,R) in our norm. It also holds for a smooth-approximation limit by passing first in each finite Fourier norm sum and then taking the supremum over finite sets. The sign-reflection map is invertible, so uniqueness and continuous dependence transfer. Finally differentiation of v=S_(-t)u cancels the linear KdV term and yields v'=B_t(v,v)/2 for smooth data; the unimodular Fourier symbol of S preserves all norms. Thus M=1+sup||v||_(H^gamma)<=1+A as asserted. This proves the asserted existence, bound, twist identity and solution convention for arbitrary q under L1; discharge L1.

For arbitrary real mean-zero L2 data q1,q2 and B0>=0, temporarily assume L2: ||q1||_2+||q2||_2<=B0. Apply E001's theta=0 dependence statement at time horizon T to -q1(-x),-q2(-x). Their norms and their difference norm are unchanged. The source twists are unitary, so its dependence bound gives sup_[0,T]||u_q1-u_q2||_2<=C(T,B0)||q1-q2||_2 in physical variables after sign-reflection. Discharge L2.

argument.text: Fix tau>0 and real alpha,beta. If either phase is zero, substitution in eta shows exact cancellation. Otherwise put h(s)=exp(-i*alpha*s)-M_tau(exp(-i*alpha*s)). The covariance is tau^(-1)integral_0^tau h(s)exp(-i*beta*s)ds. By the fundamental theorem of calculus, |exp(-i*alpha*s)-exp(-i*alpha*r)|<=|alpha||s-r|. Averaging in r gives |h(s)|<=tau|alpha|, and consequently |eta|<=tau|alpha|. Interchange alpha,beta to obtain the minimum. Also |h(0)|+|h(tau)|<=tau|alpha| and integral_0^tau|h'(s)|ds=tau|alpha|. Integrating the beta exponential once by parts gives |eta|<=(|h(0)|+|h(tau)|+integral|h'|)/(tau|beta|)<=2|alpha/beta|. Interchanging phases proves the other ratio. These arguments apply to smooth scalar exponentials, so the calculus identities have no limiting issue.

Fix nonzero integer frequencies a,b,c,d with sum zero, order their magnitudes N1>=N2>=N3>=N4, and put A=|ab|, B0=|cd|. Triangle inequality gives N1<=3N2. For the first majorant, if d is among the largest two, min(A/B0,B0/A)<=1 and 1/|d|<=1/N3. Otherwise the two largest are among a,b,c. If they are a,b, use (B0/A)/|d|=|c|/|ab|<=1/N3. If they are a,c, their ratio lies in [1/3,3], giving (1/|d|)min(A/B0,B0/A)<=3 min(|b|/|d|^2,1/|b|)<=3/max(|b|,|d|)=3/N3; the last inequality follows by dividing into |b|<=|d| and its complement. The b,c case is the identical exchange of a,b. For the second majorant, if the largest two lie in a single pair (a,b) or (c,d), the other pair sum has magnitude <=2N3, whereas max(A,B0)>=N1N2>=N3^2. Since a+b=-(c+d), the ratio is <=2/N3. If they lie in different pairs, the third largest is paired with one of them, so max(A,B0)>=N2N3 while |a+b|<=2N1<=6N2. This gives 6/N3. Ties admit any ordering and the cases still exhaust all possibilities.

locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary x1, first finitely supported and then arbitrary in ell2.
Fix arbitrary x2, first finitely supported and then arbitrary in ell2.
Fix arbitrary x3, first finitely supported and then arbitrary in ell2.
Fix arbitrary x4, first finitely supported and then arbitrary in ell2.
Define X_(r,j) as the shell ell2 norm of sequence r, with negative shell norms zero.

argument.text: Fix four finitely supported nonnegative sequences x1,x2,x3,x4 on Z\{0}. Decompose each into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, and let X_(r,j) be its ell2 norm on shell j. Fix one ordering of shell indices j1>=j2>=j3>=j4 (and correspondingly permute the input labels). Any zero-sum interaction has j1-j2<=2: the largest magnitude is at most three times the second largest, while a gap >=3 would give a ratio greater than four. For each fixed pair of the smaller frequencies, the sum over the two larger frequencies is bounded by the product of their ell2 norms, since one is a translated reflection of the other. Each small shell contains 2^(j+1) integers. Cauchy-Schwarz on the smaller shells therefore bounds the unweighted four-frequency sum by C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r X_(r,jr). Division by N3>=2^j3 leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2).

produces.statement: For all j1>=j2>=j3>=j4>=0, with j1-j2<=2, the sum over zero-sum frequencies in the respective four shells of product_r x_r(k_r)/N3(k1,k2,k3,k4) is at most C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2)*product_r X_(r,jr), where N3 is the third largest magnitude.

argument.text: Sum F001 with the offset q=j1-j2 in {0,1,2}. Dropping the upper restriction on the small shell indices only increases this positive sum, leaving at most C*(sum_J X_(1,J)X_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m)2^(-(ell-m)/2)X_(3,ell)X_(4,m)). Interpret negative shell subscripts as zero. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the first factor by ||X_1||_ell2||X_2||_ell2. In the second set r=ell-m, apply Cauchy-Schwarz to each shifted scalar product, and sum the geometric series: its bound is ||X_3||_ell2||X_4||_ell2/(1-2^(-1/2)). Sum over at most 24 shell orderings and three offsets. Since sum_j X_(r,j)^2=||x_r||_ell2^2, this proves the finite estimate. For arbitrary nonnegative square-summable inputs, restrict all four to |k|<=m. The positive sum is the increasing supremum of these finite sums and the restricted norms are bounded by the original norms; taking the supremum proves the infinite estimate. Restricting the positive summation set can only decrease it.

argument.text: Orthogonality of exp(i*k*x) in normalized measure gives the L2 Fourier norm identity on polynomials; completion gives it on L2. Unimodularity and conjugate symmetry of exp(i*t*k^3) give unitarity, reality and mean preservation of S directly in Fourier coefficients. Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infty<=(sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2, and ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. More generally H^1 embeds in L^infty by the same summable reciprocal weights. For A0,B0 in H^1, the product rule together with this embedding gives ||A0 B0||_(H^1)<=C||A0||_(H^1)||B0||_(H^1), first on polynomials and then by density. Apply this to the two inverse derivatives to obtain the J bound. The Fourier coefficient of a product of two L2 functions is bounded by the product of their L2 norms by Cauchy-Schwarz. Therefore ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-p_star))^2<=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0) k^2<k>^(-2*p_star), and this series converges because p_star=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum k^(-2) gives ||Dinv P(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. On mean-zero coefficients <k>^(-p_star)<=|k|^(-1), so the negative-norm comparison follows. In J_t(A0,B0), bound its first inverse derivative in L2 and its second in L^infty to get the asymmetric bound. All constants are uniform in t since S is an isometry. Bounded-product extensions follow by the displayed estimates and density.

For smooth mean-zero paths f,g the nonzero kth Fourier coefficient of J_t(f,g) is sum_(a+b=k) exp(-i*3*k*a*b*t)(i*a)^(-1)(i*b)^(-1) hat f(a)hat g(b). Differentiating the phase contributes 3*i*k times the product coefficient. Thus partial_t J_t(f,g)=3 B_t(f,g)+J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g'). Integrate in time and divide by three to obtain the normal-form identity with both endpoints. Smooth spatial Fourier series and their derivatives converge absolutely, justifying the differentiation. J is symmetric. In J_t(B_t(f,g),h), Dinv B_t(f,g)=S_(-t)P[(S_t f)(S_t g)], since Dinv*partial_x=P. Substitution, without commuting any operator through a product, gives the stated Cint identity after integration. The calculation holds on each smooth time piece, so summing preserves both external endpoints. For time-independent f set g=f and divide the integral by two; this yields Stage(t;f)=[J_s(f,f)]/6.

Use N010 with a constant C_M enlarged to work throughout this ball. Define N=ceil(max(2,8*C_M,(8*C_M)^(14/23))). Then C_M(N^(-1)+N^(-23/14))<=1/4. Then choose delta in (0,1] so small that C_M delta(N^2+3)<=1/4, and restrict tau<=delta/2. On any interval starting at a grid point and of length h<=delta with error supremum <=1, N010 absorbs the error coefficient: h+tau<=3delta/2, and hence E_I<=2||e(a)||_2+C'_M delta*tau^gamma. These choices depend only on the common M and gamma,T.

argument.text: Partition the grid into blocks of floor(delta/tau) steps and a possibly shorter final block. Full block lengths belong to [delta/2,delta], so there are at most 2T/delta+1 blocks. Iterate F001, beginning with e(0)=0, to get sup_[0,t]||e||_2<=K*tau^gamma on every prefix on which ||e||_2<=1; K depends only on T,gamma,R. This includes a prefix ending inside the last step, because N010 explicitly allows a partial final interval. N007 gives continuity of the interpolant; the exact solution is continuous by N001. For contradiction assume L2: the error first reaches one at a time in [0,T]. At that first time, the same finite recurrence through that first time would give <=K*tau^gamma. Choose tau0<=min(1,delta/2) so small that K*tau0^gamma<1/2, possible because H002 gives gamma>0. This contradicts L2, which is discharged; hence the estimate holds on all [0,T]. N007 gives V(t_n)=S_(-t_n)u^n and N001 gives unitarity of the twist, so the grid-point bound follows. No bound depends on higher smooth norms or spectral support. argument.text: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau is continuous from mean-zero L2 to L2. Indeed N005 gives Dinv:L2->H^1 and the H^1 product bound; consequently F_tau:L2->H^1 is a continuous quadratic map. The first term of H_tau is a product of inverse derivatives. Its second has the continuous bilinear scalar mean P0(f^2) multiplied by S_tau Dinv f. Its third is the H^1 product (S_s Dinv f)^3 followed by Dinv. Its fourth is the product of D^(-2)F_tau(f) and Dinv f, with unitary S factors and a final D^(-2). Each is continuous into L2; all scalar coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for this fixed tau. Hence the map and all of its finitely many iterates are continuous. The same formulas preserve reality and zero mean: explicit P, outer inverse derivatives, and the zero-mean factor in the scalar-mean term show this directly.

argument.text: Take C,tau0 from N011, determined only by T,gamma,R. Fix an arbitrary positive integer L with tau=T/L<=tau0. Applying N011 to u0_m gives the same error bound C*tau^gamma for every m. By F002 the numerical iterates converge in L2 at each of the finitely many grid points, and F001 gives uniform convergence of the exact solutions. The reverse triangle inequality, followed by the maximum over L+1 points, passes the estimate to u0. Since C and tau0 depend only on T,gamma,R, their choice is uniform over the entire datum ball and all L, this is the full conclusion P, including n=0. The finite-step continuity argument uses fixed tau only and imposes no support restriction or numerical H^gamma bound.
